ORAL JUDGMENT :-
1. Heard.
2. ADMIT.
Heard finally by the consent of learned Counsel for the Applicants and learned APP for the Non-applicant No.1/State.

3. Despite service none appears for the Non-applicant No.2.
4.

The present Application is preferred by the Applicants who are the in-laws and sister-in-law of the Non-applicant No.2 under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the First Information Report in connection with Crime No.124/2022 registered with Police Station Barshitakli, District Akola for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
3 50A.APL.659-2022.JUDGMENT.odt 5.
The crime is registered on the basis of a report lodged by the Non-applicant No.2 on an allegation that her marriage was performed with the son of the Applicant Nos. 1 and 2.

After marriage she resumed cohabitation but she was illtreated by the present Applicants by demanding the amount as well as by saying that if she has not brought the money they will perform the second marriage otherwise she has to give divorce to her husband.
It is alleged by her that, her father was not able to fulfill the said demand, and therefore, she constrained to leave the matrimonial house.
On the basis of the said report Police have registered the crime against the present Applicants.

6. Heard learned Counsel for the Applicants, who submitted that, except general and sweeping allegations no specific instances are narrated to attract the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC.
He further submitted that, this FIR came to be lodged only to give a counter blasts to the counter FIR registered by the Applicant No.2.
He submitted that, the Applicant No.3 got married in the year 2011 i.e. long before the marriage of the Non-applicant No.2.
There is no occasion for 4 50A.APL.659-2022.JUDGMENT.odt her to visit the parents house and illtreat the present Non-applicant No.2.
He submitted that, merely because she is the relative of the husband she is implicated in the alleged offence.
In view of that, the Application deserves to be allowed.

7. Per contra, learned APP strongly opposed the said contentions and submitted that there are specific allegations levelled against the present Applicants, and therefore, the Application deserves to be rejected.
8.
After hearing both the sides and on perusal of the entire investigation papers, admittedly, except the bare statement, there are no specific instances narrated.

As far as the overt act or the conduct of the present Applicants are concerned, general, omnibus and vague allegations are levelled against Sahadeo S/O Rajaram Prabhe And 2 Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Barshitakli ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20437143/

Now, it is well settled that, mere reference of the names of the relatives without assigning any specific role or specific instance is not sufficient to attract the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC.
9. Section 498-A of IPC deals with the husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.
The 5 50A.APL.659-2022.JUDGMENT.odt
Explanation

given under Section 498-A of IPC which states as under:
"Explanation.--For the purpose of this Section

, "cruelty"
means-(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

10. There is no doubt that the object of introducing Chapter XX-A containing Section 498-A in the Indian Penal Code was to prevent the torture to a woman by her husband or by relatives of her husband.

In any event the willful act of conduct ought to be the proximate cause in order to bring home the charge under Section 498-A.
11.

In the light of the above requirement if the facts and circumstances of the present case are taken into consideration, except general and sweeping allegations, no specific instances are narrated to constitute the offence punishable under Section 6 50A.APL.659-2022.JUDGMENT.odt 498-A of IPC.
In view of that, the Application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order.

ORDER i. Criminal Application is allowed.
ii. The First Information Report in connection with Crime No. 124/2022 registered with Police Station Barshitakli, District Akola for the offence punishable under Sections 498, 323, 504 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, is hereby quashed and set aside to the extent of the present Applicants.
12. Pending application/s, if any, shall stand disposed of accordingly.
